findings.title: Full-time exclusivity
findings.deviation: The clause requires the contractor to work exclusively for AtliQ and prohibits any other engagements.
findings.impact: This creates a risk of the contractor being misclassified as an employee and is a restriction AtliQ would not accept from its own clients.
findings.quote: During the term of this Agreement, the Contractor shall devote his professional working time exclusively to the Company and shall not, directly or indirectly, provide services to, or be engaged or employed by, any other person, firm or company, whether paid or unpaid, without the Company's prior written consent.
findings.counterPosition: Delete exclusivity clause; freelancers should be permitted to provide services to other clients provided there is no conflict of interest.

findings.title: Worldwide non-compete
findings.deviation: The clause imposes a 12-month worldwide non-compete on the freelancer.
findings.impact: Such broad restrictions on a contractor's ability to work are generally unenforceable and exceed the playbook's limits on restrictive covenants.
findings.quote: For a period of twelve (12) months after termination or expiry of this Agreement, the Contractor shall not, anywhere in the world, directly or indirectly, provide any software or data services to any person, whether as an employee, consultant, contractor, partner or otherwise, in competition with the Company.
findings.counterPosition: Delete the non-compete; limit restrictions to non-solicitation of AtliQ's staff.

findings.title: One-sided notice periods
findings.deviation: AtliQ has a 24-hour termination right while the contractor must provide 60 days' notice.
findings.impact: The notice periods are extremely imbalanced and do not meet the 15-day mutual standard for freelancer agreements.
findings.quote: The Company may terminate this Agreement at any time by giving twenty-four (24) hours' written notice (including by email) to the Contractor. ... The Contractor may terminate this Agreement by giving sixty (60) days' written notice to the Company.
findings.counterPosition: Make the notice period mutual (e.g., 15 days).

findings.title: One-sided liability cap
findings.deviation: The liability cap only protects AtliQ and is set at 3 months of fees rather than the standard 12 months.
findings.impact: The contractor remains exposed to unlimited liability while AtliQ's liability is strictly limited.
findings.quote: The Company's liability to the Contractor shall not exceed the fees payable for the preceding three (3) months.
findings.counterPosition: Make the cap mutual and set it at 1x fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim.

findings.title: One-way uncapped indemnity
findings.deviation: The contractor provides an indemnity for breach of contract, but AtliQ provides no reciprocal indemnity.
findings.impact: The contractor is required to indemnify AtliQ for direct losses without any reciprocal protection for the contractor's own risks.
findings.quote: The Contractor shall indemnify the Company against losses arising from the Contractor's breach of Clauses 6 or 7 or his wilful misconduct.
findings.counterPosition: Provide mutual indemnities for third-party claims arising from a party's negligence or breach, subject to the liability cap.

findings.title: Discretionary exchange rate
findings.deviation: AtliQ determines the currency conversion rate at its sole discretion.
findings.impact: The contractor faces unpredictable financial risk as AtliQ can unilaterally decide the value of the payment in Indian Rupees.
findings.quote: All fees are stated in United States Dollars but shall be paid in Indian Rupees by bank transfer, converted at an exchange rate determined by the Company at its discretion on the date of payment.
findings.counterPosition: Use a verifiable market reference rate (e.g., the XE.com or central bank rate) for currency conversion.

findings.title: Discretionary timesheet approval
findings.deviation: The project manager has absolute discretion to approve or reject timesheets.
findings.impact: This allows AtliQ to withhold payment for work performed without objective grounds, which AtliQ would reject if proposed by a client.
findings.quote: The Company's project manager shall review and approve timesheets at his discretion.
findings.counterPosition: Approval should not be unreasonably withheld or delayed for work performed in accordance with the agreement.

findings.title: Unclear payment for WIP
findings.deviation: Payment upon termination is limited to 'approved hours', which may exclude work in progress.
findings.impact: If AtliQ terminates for convenience, the contractor might not be paid for work performed between the last timesheet and the termination date.
findings.quote: On termination, the Company shall pay for approved hours up to the termination date in accordance with Clause 4.
findings.counterPosition: Ensure payment for all services performed up to the date of termination, including work in progress.

findings.title: Missing breach notification
findings.deviation: The 72-hour security breach notification required by Lakeshore Grocers is not passed down to the contractor.
findings.impact: AtliQ may be unable to meet its 72-hour reporting obligation to Lakeshore if the contractor does not report incidents immediately.
findings.quote: The Contractor shall perform the Services diligently and to a professional standard, and comply with the Company's reasonable instructions, security policies and the policies of the Company's clients notified to him.
findings.counterPosition: Add a specific requirement for the contractor to notify AtliQ of any data incident within 24-48 hours.
findings.linkedQuote: Vendor shall notify Lakeshore within seventy-two (72) hours of discovering any unauthorized access to Lakeshore Data.

findings.title: Non-solicitation of clients
findings.deviation: The clause prohibits the contractor from accepting work from AtliQ's clients independently.
findings.impact: This is a 'client-capture' provision that AtliQ's playbook explicitly flags as a term to never accept from a client.
findings.quote: For a period of twelve (12) months after termination or expiry, the Contractor shall not solicit or accept work from any client of the Company for whom he performed Services...
findings.counterPosition: Limit non-solicitation to AtliQ's employees only.

findings.title: Missing insurance limits
findings.deviation: The specific insurance limits required by Lakeshore are not mandated for the contractor.
findings.impact: AtliQ may face a gap in coverage if the contractor's negligence causes a loss exceeding their personal means and they lack the client-required insurance.
findings.quote: The Contractor is responsible for his own taxes, insurance and statutory compliance.
findings.counterPosition: Require the contractor to maintain professional liability and general liability insurance at levels sufficient to cover their potential indemnity obligations.
findings.linkedQuote: Vendor shall maintain commercial general liability ($1,000,000) and professional liability ($2,000,000) insurance.

fine.note: IP assignment language is robust and vests work product in AtliQ upon creation, meeting the standard for a buyer.
The 5-year confidentiality survival period and standard exclusions are acceptable for a freelancer agreement.
No liquidated damages are imposed on the contractor, which is favorable for AtliQ's paper.
